On Revision

The first draft is just you telling yourself the story. The real work begins when you shape that story for someone else.

I revise obsessively. Not because I'm insecure, but because I know the gap between what I meant and what I wrote. Revision closes that gap.

The best revision feels invisible. The reader never sees the scaffolding. They just experience the building.

Three rules I follow: cut 10%, then cut another 10%. Read it backwards to catch errors. And never fall in love with a sentence — if it doesn't serve the whole, it goes.
